claims.text: Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles have a broad premelting regime governed by local compositional fluctuations.
Local compositional fluctuations arise during reduction of the solid precursor.
Limited atomic mobility produces spatially heterogeneous elemental distributions.
Compositionally heterogeneous regions have locally reduced cohesive energy.
Regions with reduced cohesive energy melt at lower temperatures than the rest of the nanoparticle.
The starting Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are uniform, fully mixed solid solutions.
Free atomic mobility is restricted in a solid precursor.
The five elements reduce stepwise or consecutively rather than cooperatively.
Differential reduction kinetics among the five elements generate persistent spatial fluctuations in elemental distribution.
Clusters enriched in low-cohesive-energy elements initiate localized premelting.
Monometallic and simpler binary nanoparticles have minimal compositional fluctuations relative to the five-element nanoparticles.
Five-element mixtures can form a single-phase random alloy despite consecutive elemental reduction.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles will begin localized melting at a lower temperature than monometallic or binary baseline nanoparticles.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles will exhibit a broader distribution of melting events than the baseline nanoparticles.
Baseline monometallic or binary nanoparticles will melt more abruptly and uniformly.
The proposed mechanism is applicable specifically to syntheses with restricted atomic mobility, such as solid-precursor reduction.
Enhanced atomic mobility in solution-based synthesis may suppress compositional fluctuations.
A lack of earlier and broader melting relative to the baseline, or a lack of spatial correlation between compositional heterogeneity and melting initiation, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial nanoparticles are described as uniform and fully mixed, while the central mediator is nanoscale segregation or clustering attributed to their formation. The hypothesis does not explain when or how a uniform initial state becomes compositionally heterogeneous.
